answer: One approach is a stake-bonded entry inlet: each new agent locks a modest, refundable deposit in a shared vault before it can transact. The bond is cheap for one honest participant but multiplies with every extra identity, so spawning thousands of sock-puppets quickly becomes unaffordable. Good behavior earns the stake back with a small yield, while proven sybil activity forfeits it. The mechanism prices identity creation instead of banning it outright, much like a sonnet's strict meter disciplines every line: the constraint channels agents toward honesty without any central gatekeeper.
